claim: For the two-layer generalized Mycielski graph \(M_2(C_5)\), the game chromatic number is exactly \(\chi_g(M_2(C_5))=4\). Equivalently, Bob can prevent completion with three colors, while Alice has a winning strategy with four colors in the standard vertex-coloring game. The four-color upper bound is certified by an exhaustive minimax search over the complete finite game tree, quotiented only by the ten dihedral automorphisms of the base \(C_5\) and by global color relabeling; the same checker independently confirms the three-color lower bound.

correctness.rationale: The graph and game rules were reconstructed from the primary source. The finite proof evaluates the exact minimax recurrence from the empty position for both three and four colors. The 16-vertex, 30-edge graph is generated directly from the definition; all ten dihedral maps used for quotienting are checked to preserve adjacency, and palette canonicalization is only a global color permutation. No sampling, depth limit, numerical approximation, or timeout conclusion is used. The finalized checker returns Bob-win for three colors and Alice-win for four, establishing the equality.

Earlier cycle values summarized there concern the classical one-layer construction. Exact-phrase and semantic searches produced no stronger covering statement.
